item.text:
The archive supports two small concepts worth developing for Mara’s free community educational display. Neither is ready to show: the available venue and supplies are uncertain, and one concept also needs collaborator permission.

1. **A paper shoreline demonstration.** Show how a repeated shape can suggest a changing shoreline by moving blue paper bands against white card. The abandoned workshop describes this demonstration and prototype materials in [workshop.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/workshop.txt) and [materials.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/materials.txt). The later workshop notes specify a three-slit pattern, while an older draft says two; no authoritative signoff or finished stencil is recorded ([shape-diagram.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/folded-water/shape-diagram.txt), [old-copy.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/old-copy.txt)). The pattern is FW-7, and public display or adaptation requires the collaborator’s separate written permission, which is not recorded ([folded-water.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/folded-water.txt)).  
   **Next steps:** Ask the collaborator for written permission and clarify which pattern version to use. Confirm whether card, scissors, and tape are actually available ([craft-box.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/craft-box.txt)); otherwise, price a minimal set within the $30 cap.

2. **A short text display about changing paths and tides.** The notebook concept and draft captions could anchor a small educational display about how water levels affect familiar routes ([concept.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/concept.txt), [text-fragments.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/text-fragments.txt)). The observations are a few written field notes, explicitly not a scientific dataset; the historical claim about the inlet path needs verification against its original reference before publication ([observations.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/observations.txt), [research.txt](/tmp/work/01-projects/tide-lines/research.txt)). Mara’s private notebook and captions do not yet have consent for public display or adaptation ([tide-notes.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/tide-notes.txt)).  
   **Next steps:** Ask Mara for permission and choose whether to omit the historical claim or verify it from the original reference. If printing is useful, the archive records up to twelve black-and-white pages for $8 when the shared studio printer is available ([printing.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/printing.txt)); that availability is not guaranteed.

**Planning constraints:** Mara has one weekend, free Saturday afternoon and Sunday morning, and a $30 maximum ([request.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/request.txt), [calendar.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/calendar.txt)). The library currently has no public-display table, and no alternative venue is booked ([venue.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/venue.txt)). There is no projector or framing supply inventory, and the old print quote has expired ([other-materials.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/other-materials.txt), [printing-quote.txt](/tmp/work/04-resources/printing-quote.txt)). A practical first step for either proposal is to find a host venue and confirm materials and costs before committing.

I would not propose using the archived photographs or sound recording: the photo agreement requires separate written consent for public display, and no later consent is recorded ([photo-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/photo-terms.txt)); recording ownership and public-use permission are unconfirmed, and the recording itself is absent ([sound-terms.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/sound-terms.txt), [sound-index.txt](/tmp/work/02-assets/notes/sound-index.txt)). The general rights note also says the studio has no blanket rights to third-party contributions ([general.txt](/tmp/work/03-rights/general.txt)). No legal clearance is established in this archive.
